fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 FCC+B2 eutectic alloy or the controlled 600°C versus 750°C aging intervention.
It replaces the target L12-ordering, planar-slip, and jagged phase-boundary-tip mechanism with atomic-plane migration at stable parallel phase boundaries.
It predicts a generic toughness increase rather than the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition and the ductility minimum near 600°C.
The proposed -200°C to 800°C and broad strain-rate boundaries are unsupported and miss the approximately 550-750°C embrittlement window.
The falsification rule relies on an arbitrary percentage improvement and cannot distinguish the proposed mechanism from unrelated strengthening or toughening mechanisms.
The cited evidence concerns nano-enamel MPEAs and SPS-processed Cantor alloy, not aging-induced ordering and phase-boundary evolution in the target eutectic HEA.
explanation: The response addresses HEA toughness at a high level and mentions thermal processing and TEM, but it does not reconstruct the material, aging window, structural mediators, mechanism, baseline, or observed ductile-brittle-ductile behavior. E1 supports atomic-plane migration only in a specialized enamel-structured MPEA and does not justify generalization to arbitrary HEAs; E2 is largely irrelevant to the claimed mechanism. The experiment is also poorly discriminating because toughness changes alone do not establish phase-boundary migration as causal, and it lacks targeted observations of ordering, planar slip, dislocation pile-ups, crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips, and absence of impurity segregation.
